newsitem.title: USA: Platinum, palladium prices soar; await Russian supplies.
newsitem.headline: Platinum, palladium prices soar; await Russian supplies.

text.p: Platinum prices Monday jumped to the highest levels in two months and palladium soared to a two-year high as nervous consumers waited for Russia to start shipping supplies to the world market.
Gold rose in sympathy, but the precious metal gave back its gain by the close.
On the New York Mercantile Exchange, July platinum leaped $7.10 an ounce at $396.50, its highest level since early March before closing with a gain of $1.70 at $391.10.
June palladium rose $9.00 to $172.90, the highest since April 1995, and settled for a gain on the day of $7.50 at $171.85 an ounce.
On New York's Commodity Exchange, June gold closed 60 cents lower at $348.70 an ounce, having given back a rally to $352.20.
"Both platinum and palladium prices moved sharply higher today as the lack of both metals forced dealers around the world to scurry," said Ted Kempf, an analyst for CPM Group.
Platinum prices have been rising because Russian supplies have been suspended since December.

Russia accounts for 60 percent of world palladium supplies and 25 percent of platinum, which is mostly used in pollution control devices in automobiles and in semiconductors in computer manufacturing.

The Russians are expected to resume shipments in June, after a decree authorising export quotas was signed last week, but analysts say the supplies will not be enough to ease the tightness in physical markets any time soon.
One industry source said Russia would need to sell a massive amount of metal in the spot market to bring prices down.
Russia's platinum group metals export agency said late last week that exports of platinum and palladium were expected to resume in about two weeks.
"We are experiencing an abnormal situation. There is nothing we can do but wait until Russia resumes sales," one precious metal trader said.
Also fuelling the strength in platinum is the weakening dollar, which slid to three-month lows against the Japanese yen Monday, making the metal more attractive to Japanese investors.
